mask.description: Mask indicating the subswath number associated with valid GCOV samples. A GCOV sample is only considered valid if it is generated from fully-focused radar samples. If at least one radar sample in the averaging set is partially focused or invalid, the corresponding mask pixel will contain the value 0. GCOV pixels outside of the radar acquisition extent are filled with the value 255

inputDataExceptionMask.description: Bitwise OR of input data exception codes for each image pixel (0: no anomaly, 2: NISAR LSAR qFSP-H1 sample slip)

case.validity_rule: Inside reference boundary and both footprints; finite positive power; mask 1..numberOfSubSwaths; inputDataExceptionMask=0. Change uses intersection of date-specific valid pixels.
case.alignment: Identical native pixel grids; no interpolation or resampling.
case.claim: Observed radar backscatter change, not a flood or damage classification.
limitations: Mixed-mode flag is set; inspect processing metadata and valid coverage before analysis.
Provisional calibration and mixed-mode acquisitions; no independent dated reference validation.
Subswath and exception masks do not establish absence of layover/shadow; static terrain quality layers not yet applied.
2018 reference boundary; area is projected grid area, not a surveyed area.
Geographic clipping excludes the river corridor in this pilot; do not infer river-water change from excluded pixels.

cross_pol.note: HV is processed like HH but does not detect or grade regions. A finding changes in the same direction in HV when its HV mean change has the same sign as its HH change.

caveats: Single before/after pair: this is a difference between two dates, not a trend, and it cannot say when between them a change happened.

Radar speckle: a 5×5 boxcar mean reduces but does not remove it; small or thin regions near the ±3 dB threshold can be noise, and the filter blurs region edges by up to 2 pixels, which enlarges small regions.
Tide state, river stage and wind on water can differ between the two acquisition times; on estuaries and coasts this alone can change backscatter strongly.
Wet soil after rain, crop growth or harvest, vegetation, construction and moving ships all change backscatter; this method measures the change, not its cause.
Layover and shadow on steep slopes are not separately masked; terrain correction (RTC) reduces but does not remove these geometry effects.

Regions are detected in HH only. HV is processed the same way and shown alongside each finding for comparison; it is not used to detect or grade regions, and the two polarizations can respond differently to the same surface.
No independent reference validation yet: each region is an observed radar change, not a confirmed water, flood or damage finding.
Source data maturity is provisional (NISAR_L2_GCOV_PROVISIONAL_V1): calibration and processing may change in later releases.
Only the 40 largest of 92 change regions are listed as findings; area totals include all of them.

categories.rule: no change region; HV <= -19 dB on both dates
region median HH >= 3 dB on the date it is brighter
darker region; median HV above -19 dB before and at or below it after
brighter region; median HV at or below -19 dB before and above it after, HV rose less than 1.5 dB
brighter region; median HV rose by at least 1.5 dB
darker region; median HV fell by at least 1.5 dB
change region that fits none of the above
